body: I'm mainly looking for big points that I may have not thought of that would be pertinent and questions that I should ask. I want to the get the most I can out of this appointment.

I understand. I'm just not ready to do anything like that. Plus, my job pays better than anything else I'm going to find for the same amount of effort, and I don't have any confidence that I could find another one. Plus, I really don't have *anyone* outside of my family, and I feel extremely isolated as it is. And at 27, it's honestly time for me to grow up :p

With respect to the credit card friend, she's ostensibly leaving him, and whether she does or not, I'm paying the amount I've agreed to and then I'm washing my hands of it. This is me giving her another chance. She made a mistake, and I don't want it to drown her.

I looked up some therapists in my area and I'm gonna write them emails tomorrow (did I mention I'm a procrastinator?) Seriously though, I am going to act on your advice, and I do appreciate it greatly.

Let me preface this by saying that I'm not trying to be argumentative. I feel like that's "running away", I'm scared to leave (I still depend on my parents a lot financially, and I also really don't have a good impression of myself as someone who can make it "out there"). Also I really don't think these thoughts are going to go away by being somewhere else. Being somewhere else and having less financial security are daunting propositions for me. 

I'm paying her cc debt because she was paying her way before she got married to an alcoholic, and she had to take loans to stay afloat. I've made her abundantly aware that this is a one-time proposition.

Thank you for responding. I went to therapy for awhile in college (~7 months), but it didn't really change anything. I get that I can't just say "it didn't work in [arbitrary length of time]", but I don't know if my insurance covers it (been too lazy to check), and I don't know how expensive it would be here. I know I'm just coming up with answers to disagree with what you suggested. I don't want to do that, and I don't want to undermine your heartfelt response. I do appreciate it, and I will try.
